attacks.claim: partition_date() switched from UTC to naive local time. Workers run TZ=America/Los_Angeles and the job fires at 01:30 UTC, which is the previous calendar day in Los Angeles, so dt= partitions are off by one against the UTC dt that dashboards read.
write_success_marker runs unconditionally after the loop, even when failed > 0. Dashboards read the partition as soon as _SUCCESS appears, so a partial partition is published as complete.

attacks.claim: src.stem comes from partner-chosen SFTP filenames and is interpolated into a shell=True command on workers that hold GCS write credentials. Filenames containing shell metacharacters such as $(...), backticks, quotes or ';' would execute on the worker. The artifact shows no validation.

Object names are deterministic, nothing clears the dt prefix before a rerun, and partitions are written in place with no staging prefix or atomic swap. A rerun that produces fewer chunks leaves stale higher-numbered chunks beside fresh ones, duplicating rows in a partition readers may already have consumed. Failed mid-file runs also leave uploaded chunks in GCS and local chunks in work_dir.

The DictWriter header is frozen from the first normalised row, so a later row with extra keys raises ValueError mid-file and fails the whole file, leaving a partial chunk. attacks.claim: Per-file failures are logged and counted but never raised. The task returns normally and Airflow reports success, so a run with missing partner files raises no alert and no non-zero exit.

attacks.claim: The gsutil subprocess has no timeout or retry, and -q suppresses its output. A hung upload can stall the nightly task indefinitely, and a transient failure surfaces only as a generic CalledProcessError that does not name the object.
